description: pkix-path-builder/tests/fixtures/bettertls/README.md:98-102 instructs regenerating the baseline via `cargo test ... -- --nocapture | awk '/^\{\$/,/^\}\$/' > tests/fixtures/.../baseline-pkix-path.json`. This works today but is fragile: if any future test (or cargo test framework output) prints a line containing exactly `{` and later exactly `}`, the awk range filter slurps that too. Likewise, panic output (RUST_BACKTRACE=full prints brace-delimited lines) would corrupt the baseline. Cleaner alternatives: (1) write the discover output to a known file path inside the test (let the test do its own File::create), eliminating the pipeline entirely; (2) emit a unique start/end sentinel like `---BASELINE-BEGIN---` and `---BASELINE-END---`. Option 1 is simplest — the test prints "wrote baseline to <path>" instead of dumping to stdout, and the readme just says "run with the env var set, then commit the file". No interpreter pipeline, no fragility.
title: discover-mode regeneration via awk is fragile — depends on no test producing { on a line by itself
